K-factor SOURCED 2026-09-12, design note E.133: a direct read of Ch.18's own 'Ballistic K Factors' table (pp.84-85) gives '17 PR APCBC', MV 2900 fps (exact match), K=1686 -- replacing this row's earlier constrained-least-squares guess (K=1971). Muzzle velocity flagged: a second Wikipedia-cited source (War Office pamphlet, 1952) gives 2950 fps instead of the 2900 fps used here (from the same table as the calibration points) -- used the value matching the calibration data's own source for internal consistency, not resolved which is more authoritative; the book's own table uses 2900 fps too, corroborating this choice.

11-pt fit vs RHA at 0deg obliquity (Bird & Livingston 2001 p.60, via Wikipedia), 0.27% error. K-factor SOURCED 2026-09-12, design note E.133: a direct read of Ch.18's own 'Ballistic K Factors' table (pp.84-85) gives '17Pdr APDS', MV 3950 fps (exact match), K=1705 -- replacing this row's earlier constrained-least-squares guess (K=1514). Not resolved -- plausibly a general-service-entry-date (March) vs. this-specific-unit's-actual-issue-date (October) distinction rather than a real conflict, but not confirmed either way; both dates postdate this project's 1943 window regardless.

This project's first towed anti-tank gun (as opposed to vehicle-mounted) -- see counters/toe/pak40_1943.md and design note E.123.

4-pt fit at 30deg obliquity (same Nachrichtenblatt source as the APCBC row above), max 0.66% error. K-factor SOURCED 2026-09-12, design note E.133: a direct read of Bird & Livingston Ch.18's own 'Ballistic K Factors' table (pp.84-85) gives '75L46 APCR', MV 3247 fps (near-exact match to the 3248 fps used here), K=3395 -- replacing this row's earlier constrained-least-squares guess (K=2356). Muzzle velocity flagged: a second source (Aberdeen/British Ordnance Board test data, Hoffschmidt 1979 via panzer-war.com) gives 933 m/s instead of the 990 m/s used here -- a real, unresolved ~3% discrepancy; used the value matching the calibration data's own source for internal consistency, same practice as this project's 17pdr APCBC note; the book's own table uses 3247 fps, corroborating this choice. Family hvap76 is a stand-in curve shared across German/Soviet 75-76mm-class tungsten rounds generally (a documented limitation of the source material, not of this project's fitting code) -- this is the first German gun in this file to actually use that stand-in.

5-pt fit at 0deg obliquity (Tank Archives 'americanized 6-pounder' blog, translating Soviet Lend-Lease testing data), 0.58% error -- tighter than this project's other unpublished-K-factor towed guns (PaK 40: 2.06%, 6pdr/17pdr: not separately reported). K-factor NOT sourced -- found via the same constrained least-squares search as the 6pdr/17pdr/PaK 40 (exponent held to the 0.8-3.0 physically-plausible band); the same degenerate pattern recurred (an unconstrained search finds a much higher, non-physical exponent for a similarly tiny error), and the constrained fit's exponent (2.94) again lands near the top of the plausible band, matching PaK 40 PzGr 39's own constrained exponent (2.94) almost exactly -- flagged as a recurring pattern for guns without a published K-factor, not a new anomaly. This is a 1943-SPECIFIC entry: the M1 is a licence-built near-copy of the British 6pdr (identical L/50 barrel) but fired only the uncapped AP Shot M70 until the capped M86/M85 shell arrived in late summer 1944 (counters/toe/us_57mm_at_1943.md) -- ammo_family is ap_uncapped, NOT capped, and this row should NOT be reused for a 1944+ US 57mm entry, which should use sixpdr_57l50_apcbc instead (near-identical MV, both capped, under 1% apart). This project's first use of the ap_uncapped family for an actual fielded gun.
